```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Besides employment records (*vinculos*), the RAIS has a file with one row per
**establishment**. In **datarais** it is requested with
`type = "estabelecimentos"` and stored in the DuckDB table `rais_estab`.

## Downloading and loading

```{r load, eval=FALSE}
library(datarais)

db <- file.path(tempdir(), "rais.duckdb")

# Establishments only
rais_load(years = 2022, type = "estabelecimentos", db_path = db)

# Employment records and establishments together
rais_load(years = 2022, type = "all", db_path = db)
```

The establishment file is named `RAIS_ESTAB_PUB.7z` from 2018 onwards and
`ESTB{year}.7z` (or `Estb{year}.zip` in some years) before that. You do not need
to remember the names: `rais_layouts()` lists them and `rais_hf_files()`
shows what exists in the repository.

## A small runnable example

The chunk below uses a synthetic `rais_estab` table with the real column names.
The numbers are random.

```{r toy}
library(datarais)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(1)
db  <- tempfile(fileext = ".duckdb")
con <- rais_connect(db, quiet = TRUE)

DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "rais_estab", data.frame(
  ano                     = 2022L,
  sigla_uf                = sample(c(23L, 24L, 35L), 60, replace = TRUE),
  tamanho_estabelecimento = sample(1:4, 60, replace = TRUE),
  qtd_vinculos_ativos     = rpois(60, 12),
  ind_simples             = sample(0:1, 60, replace = TRUE)
))
```

`rais_tbl(con, type = "estabelecimentos")` returns the establishment table as a
lazy dplyr table:

```{r estab-uf}
rais_tbl(con, type = "estabelecimentos") |>
  group_by(sigla_uf) |>
  summarise(
    estabelecimentos = n(),
    vinculos_ativos  = sum(qtd_vinculos_ativos, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  left_join(uf_codigos, by = c("sigla_uf" = "codigo")) |>
  mutate(vinculos_por_estab = vinculos_ativos / estabelecimentos) |>
  arrange(desc(estabelecimentos))
```

Establishments by size class and by participation in the Simples regime:

```{r estab-size}
rais_tbl(con, type = "estabelecimentos") |>
  count(tamanho_estabelecimento, ind_simples) |>
  collect() |>
  arrange(tamanho_estabelecimento, ind_simples)
```

```{r cleanup}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
unlink(db)
```

## Main variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `ano` | Reference year |
| `sigla_uf` | State (numeric IBGE code) |
| `id_municipio` | Municipality (IBGE code) |
| `natureza_juridica` | Legal nature of the establishment |
| `tamanho_estabelecimento` | Size class by number of employees |
| `cnae20_classe`, `cnae20_subclasse` | Economic activity (CNAE 2.0) |
| `qtd_vinculos_ativos` | Active jobs on 31 December |
| `qtd_vinculos_clt`, `qtd_vinculos_estat` | Jobs by legal regime |
| `ind_simples`, `ind_participa_pat` | Simples regime and PAT indicators |

Use `rais_col_info(type = "estabelecimentos")` to see the full list, and
`rais_col_dictionary()` for the mapping from the original column names.

## Linking establishments and employment records

Both tables share `ano`, `sigla_uf`, `id_municipio` and `cnae20_classe`. The
public microdata do not carry an identifier that links a job to its
establishment, so joins are done at an aggregate level, for example jobs per
state and activity from `rais_novo` against establishments per state and
activity from `rais_estab`.

See `vignette("serie-historica", package = "datarais")` for time series built
from the employment records.
